name: split-button
purpose: A primary command button visually joined to a chevron toggle that opens an overlay menu of related actions defined by a `model` array. The primary button runs the default action; the joined toggle composes `navigation/dropdown-menu` to present the remaining actions. Opt into `updateLabelOnSelect` to have the primary segment mirror the last-chosen menu action (label + icon), turning the control into a "default is the last selection" pattern; the primary `click` then reports that mirrored action as its second argument, so a single handler can run whichever action is active. Use it when one action is the default and related actions belong in an attached menu; for a single action use `Button`, and for a standalone menu use `DropdownMenu`.
useWhen: One default action with a few related alternatives (Save and Save as draft, Deploy and Deploy to staging).
A "repeat the last choice" control: set `updateLabelOnSelect` so the primary segment mirrors the last action picked.
avoidWhen: A menu with no default action → use `dropdown-menu`.
Picking one of a few visible, mutually exclusive options → use `toggle-group`.
related: button` — the primary segment; `kind` here is limited to `primary`, `secondary` and `outlined`.
dropdown-menu` — the overlay menu the toggle composes; use it alone when there is no default action.
bestPractices: Give every `model` entry a stable `value`; without one the `label` identifies the action, so renaming it changes what handlers receive.
Handle the default action in `@click` and the menu actions in `@item-click`; both receive `(event, item)`.
With `updateLabelOnSelect`, read the second argument of `click` (the mirrored item, `null` until one is picked) to run whichever action is active.
Set `loading` while the action runs: it disables both segments and keeps the menu closed.
Disable a single action with `disabled: true` on its model entry instead of removing it, so the menu does not shift.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible label text on the primary command button.

props.name: icon
props.doc: PrimeIcons class for the primary button's leading icon.

props.name: model
props.doc: Actions rendered as rows in the attached overlay menu.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Visual variant applied to both joined segments.

props.name: size
props.doc: Size token; affects height, padding, and typography.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables both segments and prevents the menu from opening.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Shows a spinner on the primary button and takes the disabled status: both segments are disabled and the menu cannot open while it resolves.

props.name: updateLabelOnSelect
props.doc: When true, selecting a menu action updates the primary button's label and icon to mirror that action and marks it as selected in the menu. Opt-in; the mirrored action is also reported as the primary `click`'s second argument, so the consumer decides what each segment does.

events.name: click
events.notes: Fired by the primary command button on activation. `item` is the action currently mirrored on the primary segment when `updateLabelOnSelect` is on, otherwise `null`. Never fires while `disabled` or `loading`.

events.name: item-click
events.notes: Fired when a menu action is selected. `event` is the pointer/keyboard event that activated the option; `item` is the matched `model` entry. The menu cannot open while `disabled` or `loading`, so it never fires in those states.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import SplitButton from '@aziontech/webkit/split-button'

  const items = [
    { label: 'Update', value: 'update', icon: 'pi pi-refresh' },
    { label: 'Duplicate', value: 'duplicate', icon: 'pi pi-copy' },
    { label: 'Delete', value: 'delete', icon: 'pi pi-trash', disabled: true }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <SplitButton
    kind="primary"
    size="large"
    label="Save"
    icon="pi pi-check"
    :model="items"
  />
</template>
